purpose: Diagnostic replication on the existing survey, not a fresh holdout or architecture promotion gate.
system_prompt: Apply the supplied criterion to the supplied evidence. Choose exactly one listed option. Respond with only its uppercase letter, with no explanation or reasoning.
permutations: All permutations for 2-4 options, identity first. Letter slots are reassigned while semantic IDs stay fixed. Head Choice permutes dictionary insertion order; Boolean and ordinal Score order are fixed by their contract, so their head permutation test is not applicable.
decision_rule: Any semantic argmax flip rejects this prompt/readout as a permutation-stable drop-in. Passing every item is necessary, not sufficient: larger fresh labelled evidence and Track A gates remain required. No confidence-only win, tuning, training, promotion, production swap, active pruning or trading.
limitations: Previously inspected 13-question diagnostic; only six declared labels, of which some are generic/arguable.
The head and letter arms necessarily differ in input serialization and scoring architecture; this is not an isolated causal test of readout alone.
Letter softmax is conditional on the selected slots, not a calibrated correctness probability.
This is the repo's existing SemIf-inspired prompt, not an independently reproduced upstream implementation.
